scenario: Enter an age below 14, then 14, 17 and 18.
expected: Enforce the launch age floor; route minors to youth rules and adults to adult rules.

scenario: Change age after selecting adult add-ons or an adult plan.
expected: Recheck eligibility; show incompatible choices and require a valid plan review.

scenario: A youth account reaches age 18.
expected: Recheck age-dependent consent, sharing and coaching choices without silently exposing records.

scenario: Decline optional sex, body measurements or health-device access.
expected: Explain any unavailable calculation; preserve useful training and never infer missing attributes.

scenario: Select first-time lifting, advanced lifting, or imported history without comparable loads.
expected: Keep experience separate from verified performance; use a suitable calibration path and no invented starting weight.

scenario: Choose coach-directed in-season training, then enter an offseason date.
expected: Track the coach plan without automatic additions; preview any switch of training authority and preserve history.

scenario: Request strength, muscle and endurance goals with too little weekly time.
expected: Ask for priority or offer changed time/timeline; do not promise all goals or silently exceed availability.

scenario: Select core, jumping, supersets and weight-management support with different ages and main goals.
expected: Apply reviewed compatibility and total-work limits; explain unsupported combinations and offer relevant alternatives.

scenario: Accept a new plan while another block exists; repeat the accept action.
expected: Replace all future active-plan views once, archive the old block and retain completed history.

scenario: Attempt a plan replacement while a workout is active.
expected: Require a clear finish, save-partial or discard choice before replacement; preserve the active record.

scenario: Move one workout onto an occupied day; choose a cascade instead.
expected: Show every changed date, preserve required gaps and reject the entire conflicting proposal without partial changes.

scenario: Create a vacation spanning several sessions, then edit or remove one day.
expected: Show affected sessions and the scope of the edit; retain fixed dates and provide undo or confirmation.

scenario: Add a competition after the block and an adaptation proposal already exist.
expected: Recheck nearby work and invalidate stale proposals; no automatic move or obsolete load change.

scenario: Schedule two games in a week with different priorities and overlapping practices.
expected: Account for all sport commitments; avoid treating lower-priority games as free recovery days.

scenario: A season starts or ends midweek, or seasons from two sports overlap.
expected: Preview phase and authority changes with combined workload; no duplicated training or silent plan replacement.

scenario: Set different available hours by day, including a short session window.
expected: Include warm-up, rests, transitions and added work in the fit; never hide an overrun.

scenario: Travel across time zones or encounter daylight-saving and year boundaries.
expected: Keep date-only commitments and intended local training times consistent; explain any time-zone change.

scenario: Leave multiple workouts overdue, skip the last workout, or save the final workout as partial.
expected: Offer a recovery path without catch-up overload; distinguish scheduled work exhausted from every session completed.

scenario: Finish a block and choose maintenance, new goals or the same goal.
expected: Carry comparable history forward and preview the next block, dates, progression and changed assumptions.

scenario: Pause training, return after a long absence, or report illness/injury during the break.
expected: Separate maintained activity from absence; offer reviewed return options and never claim medical clearance.

scenario: Start a workout and try to mark all sets done without actual amounts.
expected: Keep targets separate; require actual completed reps or time and preserve unknown loads.

scenario: Enter blank, zero, fractional reps, negative, huge or pasted malformed amounts.
expected: Show a field-specific error; count metrics use valid whole counts and decimals remain available where appropriate.

scenario: Change lb/kg units around an active workout and round-trip historical records.
expected: Preserve canonical values, unit labels and practical precision; never convert an already converted value twice.

scenario: Log paired dumbbells, one-arm rows, alternating curls and per-leg split squats.
expected: State whether load is per hand or total and whether reps are per side; volume uses the exact convention once.

scenario: Log only one side or unequal loads/reps on the two sides.
expected: Retain separate side records; do not invent the other side or reuse incompatible progression history.

scenario: Change cable ratio, machine model, seat setting or assistance amount.
expected: Record setup and assistance separately; do not compare incompatible loads or rank them as equivalent work.

scenario: Record bodyweight, added load, assistance, bands, jumps, timed drills and running intervals.
expected: Show appropriate primary and optional metrics; do not apply ordinary loaded-rep progression to every modality.

scenario: Create a custom movement, add it across a block, then change its logging convention.
expected: Review time and affected sessions; preserve old meaning in history and require eligibility before automatic progression.

scenario: Run a superset, pause rest, leave the app, reopen, or complete another set.
expected: Maintain understandable rest timing and order; never mark work complete from a timer alone.

scenario: Save partial work, resume or repeat it, correct a past entry, or tap Finish twice.
expected: Save each actual exposure once, preserve revisions and distinguish the repeat from the original partial work.

scenario: Reach the top of a rep range with easy RIR across the required comparable exposures.
expected: Use the reviewed progression rule and available increment; clearly distinguish accepted scheduled progression from a new feedback change.

scenario: Report easy effort but incomplete reps, unknown load, changed setup or old history.
expected: Do not infer readiness from one favorable signal; explain why calibration or more comparable work is needed.

scenario: Available plates or dumbbells force a larger increase than the reviewed limit.
expected: Keep the present load or offer a reviewed alternative; never recommend an unavailable or excessive increment.

scenario: Report pain, uncertain symptoms, severe soreness or unexpectedly reduced performance.
expected: Separate symptoms from ordinary effort; hold affected automated advice and provide an appropriate non-diagnostic path.

scenario: Accept, decline, queue, reopen or reaccept a suggestion after records or dates change.
expected: Apply only a current proposal once; show the full change and leave the accepted plan intact when declined.

scenario: Choose low exercise enjoyment while performance is improving.
expected: Treat preference as preference; show substitutions that preserve purpose without silently discarding a stable main lift.

scenario: Choose true powerlifting, bodybuilding, powerbuilding, running or a specific sport/position.
expected: Provide a genuinely supported reviewed program; label foundations and unsupported position-specific coverage honestly.

scenario: Review estimated 1RM, session volume and the personal score with partial or sparse history.
expected: Use eligible data and visible methods; missing values are not zero, youth exclusions work and the score is not a validated ability rank.

scenario: Cancel Google login, link an existing identity, or switch accounts on a shared device.
expected: Return safely and show only the authenticated account data; linking requires verified ownership.

scenario: Lose a passkey/device, change biometrics, exhaust MFA attempts or reuse a recovery code.
expected: Provide verified recovery without bypassing protection; revoke or consume credentials correctly and never collect biometrics.

scenario: Two users request the same record, photo, export or coach endpoint using changed IDs.
expected: Server authorization blocks cross-account access for every operation, including signed media links.

scenario: A youth shares selected dates/categories with a parent or coach, then revokes access.
expected: Enforce the actual scope and read/edit distinction; revoke future access without claiming downloaded copies can be recalled.

scenario: Install on a second device and edit the same workout offline on both.
expected: Use record versions and idempotency; surface conflicts and preserve both actual inputs until resolved.

scenario: Local storage is full, corrupt or unavailable during logging, followed by app termination.
expected: Report unsaved changes immediately; preserve recoverable data and offer tested export/retry/recovery.

scenario: Log out, delete an account, restore a backup or reinstall on a shared phone.
expected: Handle local caches, server records, backups and credentials according to explicit retention rules with clear user outcomes.

scenario: Deny camera access, choose limited photos, upload a very large file, or delete a progress photo.
expected: Keep training usable; validate uploads, remove unnecessary location metadata and enforce private access/deletion behavior.

scenario: Export or import malformed, huge, duplicate or instruction-bearing AI plan/history data.
expected: Validate a bounded schema, preview changes and provenance, reject executable instructions and avoid duplicate history.

scenario: An expired session or revoked sharing token is used while the phone reconnects.
expected: Reauthorize queued actions before applying them; never upload or reveal data under a different identity.

scenario: Complete setup, logging and adaptation review with keyboard and screen readers.
expected: Labels, focus order, states and errors are understandable; all core actions remain operable.

scenario: Close a guide/dialog with Escape, Android Back, VoiceOver escape or an iOS dismissal gesture.
expected: Preserve the draft and restore context/focus; keep modal errors visible within the active surface.

scenario: Use the largest native text and web zoom on small phones, landscape and split-screen.
expected: Keep content and actions readable without clipping or obscured focus; respect safe areas and the keyboard.

scenario: Tap Done, close, delete, retry and equipment filters one-handed during a workout.
expected: Meet the chosen touch-target sizes with no overlapping targets; important actions have clear labels and recovery.

scenario: Search an unfamiliar name, equipment subtype or muscle and receive no results.
expected: Offer clear filters/search recovery and custom creation; keep machine, cable, barbell, dumbbell and kettlebell variants distinct.

scenario: Open every published exercise guide, including a custom exercise and unavailable media.
expected: Show accurate self-setup, execution, finish and load rules; label missing instructions/videos and provide useful fallbacks.

scenario: A beginner follows written cues or watches an exercise demonstration without sound.
expected: Use plain language while retaining exercise terms; captions and exact-variant visuals explain the movement without claiming form assessment.

scenario: Read charts, status colors, alerts and animations with assistive technology or reduced motion enabled.
expected: Provide equivalent data tables and text status; maintain contrast and honor reduced motion without losing meaning.

scenario: Grant only some HealthKit/Health Connect permissions, later revoke them, or reconnect a provider.
expected: Respect per-type consent; show what is unavailable and keep core tracking functional without repeated coercive prompts.

scenario: Receive the same session from a watch, Strava and manual entry, including late corrections.
expected: Reconcile source IDs, timestamps and provenance without duplicate volume or overwrite of deliberate manual corrections.

scenario: Receive absent, stale or implausible heart-rate, distance or readiness data from a device.
expected: Display quality/time context and exclude unreliable inputs from automated decisions; absence is not a zero value.

scenario: A partner API is unavailable, rate-limited or removes required access.
expected: Use bounded retries and visible last-sync state; disable unsupported claims and preserve user data.

scenario: Use a public API token with wrong scope, revoked status or a repeated import request.
expected: Enforce authentication, least-privilege scopes, rate limits and idempotency; provide auditable import outcomes.

scenario: Deploy a bad app/backend version or restore a production backup during an outage.
expected: Exercise rollback and restore procedures; retain valid records and compatibility with supported clients.

scenario: Inspect logs, crash reports, notifications and analytics after sensitive actions.
expected: Exclude secrets and unnecessary health details; ensure approved diagnostics still reveal failures and account-safe support context.

scenario: A content source changes, a video license expires, or a coaching rule is withdrawn.
expected: Trace affected entries/plans, stop new unsupported recommendations and deliver reviewed replacements without rewriting actual history.
